August climatology typically delivers highs of 12–13°C under cool southerly and westerly maritime flows, but a developing front and brief northerly shift are expected to allow modest warming while sustained cloud cover and winds cap further gains. Recent days stayed cooler at 10–12°C amid stronger southerlies, so the latest model runs reflect improving conditions. Small differences in frontal timing or wind direction can shift the observed peak by 1°C, keeping the market tightly contested ahead of final MetService guidance.

**Current short-range forecasts from sources like BBC Weather, timeanddate.com, and EaseWeather place Warsaw’s high on August 13 near 24–25 °C under partly sunny skies, light northeasterly winds, and negligible precipitation.** Numerical weather models (ECMWF, GFS) show stable high pressure and modest warm advection, keeping daytime maxima in the mid-20s Celsius—consistent with the market’s heavy weighting toward 24 °C (49.5 %) and the adjacent 23 °C / 25 °C outcomes.

August climatology for Warsaw centers on highs of ~23–24 °C, so the present pattern represents near-normal late-summer conditions rather than an anomalous heat event. Minor model spread—some runs peaking at 23 °C, others briefly touching 25 °C—explains the tight probability cluster; longer-range ensembles still show low risk of either a strong cold front or amplified ridging that would push extremes outside 22–26 °C.

Traders are therefore pricing the most likely verified maximum from official Polish Institute of Meteorology observations, with the 24 °C bin capturing the highest-confidence consensus two days before the measurement window closes.
